etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French divin, from Latin dīvīnus (“of a god”), from divus (“god”). Displaced native Old English godcund.

definitions.definition: Of or pertaining to a god.

quote.text: Yet oft his heart, divine of something ill, / Misgave him.

definitions.definition: (obsolete, of souls) immortal; elect or saved after death

quote.text: (Of that at leaſure) but the bloody ſtageOn which to act, Generall this night is thine,Thou lyeſt downe mortall, who muſt riſe diuine.

quote.text: The first divines of New England  […]  were surpassed by none in extensive erudition.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Replaced Middle English devine, devin from Middle French deviner, from Latin dīvīnō.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To foretell (something), especially by the use of divination.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To guess or discover (something) through intuition or insight.
